turns.learner: Hello! Can you give me an exercise on comparatives (-er, more ... than)?
turns.tutor:
Here is the rule: short words add -er (easy - easier); long words use more; then add than.
Right: "A horse is heavier than a dog." Wrong: "A horse is heavyer than a dog." With a y at the end, change y to i, then add -er.
My example: "A tiger is more dangerous than a cat." Step 1: is dangerous short or long? Long. Step 2: so I use more. Step 3: then than.
Now you try. Complete:
"Cairo is ___ (big) than Luxor."
